definitions.explanation: An imposing power or presence that inspires awe, respect, or fear in others. Usually associated with rulers, leaders, or institutions of authority.

examples.english: To submit to the king's authority.

examples.japanese: ⟦{長年|ながねん}→長年：09684_naganen⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{経験|けいけん}→経験：01179_keiken⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{彼|かれ}→彼：01292_kare⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧{揺|ゆ}るぎない{威|い}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{与|あた}えていた→与える：01821_ataeru⟧。
examples.english: Long years of experience had given him unshakeable authority.

notes:
A literary, somewhat archaic noun rarely used on its own in modern conversation. Most commonly encountered as a component of compounds or set expressions.

COMPOUNDS:
- ⟦{威厳|いげん}→威厳：10680_igen⟧: dignity; majesty
- ⟦{威力|いりょく}→威力：19611_iryoku⟧: power; might
- ⟦{権威|けんい}→権威：13173_keni⟧: authority (institutional)
- ⟦{威信|いしん}→威信：12259_ishin⟧: prestige; standing
- {示威|じい}: demonstration (of force)

COMMON EXPRESSIONS:
- ⟦{虎|とら}→虎：02228_tora⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{威|い}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{借|か}る→借りる：00532_kariru⟧⟦{狐|きつね}→狐：04337_kitsune⟧: 'a fox borrowing a tiger's authority' — a person who bullies others by relying on a powerful backer
